slides.label: Part 1 · Job description
slides.title: Its role, its tone, its limits.
slides.body: Written down, like you would for a new hire.
slides.you: "Answer inquiries. Book calls. Never quote custom pricing."

slides.label: Part 2 · Tools
slides.title: The apps it's allowed to use.
slides.body: Inbox, calendar, CRM, accounting. No access, no work.

slides.label: Part 3 · Trigger
slides.title: What starts the work.
slides.body: A new email. A form submission. 8 a.m. every Monday.

slides.label: Part 4 · Approval point
slides.title: Where it stops and asks.
slides.body: Before it sends, pays or publishes anything, a person says yes.

slides.label: How to start
slides.title: Hire one, not ten.
slides.body: Pick the task your team dreads most. Give it all 4 parts. Keep approvals on for two weeks.

caption:
Hiring an AI employee? It needs 4 things or it fails.

1. A job description: its role, tone and limits
2. Tools: the apps it's allowed to use
3. A trigger: what starts the work
4. An approval point: where it stops and asks a person

Number 4 is the one people skip. Without a checkpoint nobody trusts the output, so nobody uses it.
